rationale:
Evidence. Across 540 trials, every run ended off track after exactly one line-loss event, and max_error sits at about 0.061 m, which is the censored off-track limit. Oval progress has been 0.115 in almost every design. The best raced design is iteration 8 (score 50.39): five sensors at y = 0.06 m, x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, 0.016 m footprint, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m, kp 2.0, ki 1.0, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.4, search_right.

What I kept from the round-1 critique. (a) Speed is not the lever: oval progress was flat from base_speed 1.0 to 1.8, so the draft's slip-out hypothesis is rejected and base_speed stays at 1.4. (b) The 0.7 speed in the draft is rejected because it is untested and gives no gain in the evidence. The stall-rule worry is weak at this speed, since 0.5 s of motion covers far more than 0.002 of the course. (c) The first failure is probably a start or first-contact condition. I cannot change start handling with these inputs, so this step does not test it. (d) The footprint, mass and wheel_track changes are dropped, since they were untested or confounded.

What I rejected from the critique. The critique says kd is always harmful because it saturates the wheels. The data do not support that: going from kd 0.1 to 0.05 (iteration 6 against iteration 3) cut s-bend progress from 0.148 to 0.040 and score from 49.94 to 35.65. So kd has a measurable effect on the s-bend in this geometry. A saturation estimate: with the 0.5 weight steps, the signal derivative at a tape edge is roughly 10 to 20 per second. At kd 0.2 that is 2 to 4 turn units, about 700 to 1400 PWM, which stays under the 4095 clamp.

Change. A single variable: kd 0.1 to 0.2, from the best raced design. Everything else matches iteration 8, so any change in result can be attributed to kd.

Expected result (a guess). s-bend progress rises a little above 0.15, and the first line-loss step moves later or stays the same. If the first-loss step and oval progress are unchanged (about 0.115), the gains are not the cause. The next revision should then test start handling and check controller_errors and the first 0.5 s of per-step telemetry. If s-bend progress falls or steering_oscillation rises sharply, kd should return to 0.1.

Metrics to read: first-loss step, progress at first loss, steering_oscillation, controller_errors, and the s-bend progress change. max_error is censored at about 0.061 m on failed runs, so it is not a pass test.
